test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following methods helps the easier assembly and disassembly by providing a more efficient way to fit the connecting rod around the crankshaft journal, particularly in tight engine compartment, in an internal combustion engine?

options.text: Big end split orthogonally on a connecting rod
Small end trimming linearly on a connecting rod
Big end split obliquely on a connecting rod
Small end union linearly on a connecting rod

solution:
The correct answer is __Big end split obliquely on a connecting rod**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Big end split obliquely__ on a connecting rod allows for easier assembly and disassembly.
 
• This design ensures better fitment around the crankshaft journal, especially in compact engine compartments.
 
• It also minimizes the risk of misalignment during assembly.
 
• Oblique splitting provides more contact area, ensuring better load distribution.
 
• It helps in reducing vibrations and improving the overall efficiency of the engine.
 
• This design is particularly advantageous in high-performance engines where precision and durability are critical.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Big end split orthogonally:**
 
 
• Orthogonal splitting is simpler but less efficient in tight spaces.
 
• It may result in higher vibrations and uneven load distribution.
 
 
 
• **Small end trimming linearly:**
 
 
• Not commonly used for disassembly purposes.
 
• Primarily involves shaping the small end for specific design requirements.
 
 
 
• **Small end union linearly:**
 
 
• Primarily relates to the attachment of the piston pin.
 
• Does not significantly impact disassembly around the crankshaft.
